mainText: Good morning, Landon. Here's your brief for Monday, November 23, 2026. Let's start with the markets. Stocks took a steep fall on Friday. The S&P 500 dropped 3.7 percent to close at 6,910. The Dow lost about 950 points, or 1.9 percent, to finish at 48,147. The Nasdaq sank 5.3 percent to 22,618. The main driver was a sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks, as investors questioned AI spending and valuations. For the week, the S&P 500 fell 8.6 percent, the Dow fell 8 percent, and the Nasdaq fell 10 percent. The S&P 500 is now in correction territory, more than 10 percent below its early October record. Stock futures bounced back Sunday evening, with Dow futures up roughly 800 points and Nasdaq futures up close to 3 percent. On the Fed, the target range for the federal funds rate sits at 3.75 to 4 percent after the October hold. Futures markets tracked by the CME FedWatch tool now price close to a certain quarter point rate hike at the December 8 and 9 meeting. J.P. Morgan has dropped its forecast for a single hike and now expects further increases in January and March of next year, according to a client note reported by Reuters. Bank of America and Deutsche Bank are also calling for a series of hikes. The Fed's Beige Book report on regional business conditions is due Wednesday afternoon. Next, Nvidia. Reuters reports that the Securities and Exchange Commission is examining potential accounting issues at the chipmaker, citing people briefed on the matter. Nvidia shares fell about 13 percent on Friday after that report. Next, a possible cybersecurity mega deal. Bloomberg and Reuters report that CrowdStrike is in talks to acquire Zscaler. The talks are described as preliminary and may not lead to a deal. Zscaler shares jumped in after hours trading, while CrowdStrike shares slipped. And finally, California Attorney General Rob Bonta is preparing his own antitrust review of DoorDash's proposed 17 billion dollar purchase of Instacart, according to Politico. The Justice Department is also reviewing the deal. On the calendar today, it's a light day for economic data in a holiday shortened week. After the closing bell, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Zoom, Agilent, Jacobs Solutions, and Symbotic report earnings. Looking ahead, Dell, Best Buy, and HP report Tuesday, and the big releases, including the PCE inflation gauge, GDP, durable goods, and jobless claims, all arrive Wednesday morning. Markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and close early on Friday. Here's your fun fact. The world's first organized futures exchange was not in Chicago or London. It was the Dojima Rice Exchange in Osaka, Japan, officially recognized by the shogunate in 1730. Samurai were paid in rice, and merchants there traded standardized contracts on future rice harvests, more than a century before Chicago's futures market opened. Have a great day.
